value:
Soak-exit policy for release cycles, codified from v1.14 (2026-05-05); exit gate rewritten 2026-07-22 — the fleet policy ([[project.surfaceStrategy]]) made the old '>=10 distinct MCP sessions' criterion unsatisfiable.

RULE: soak runs to a HARD cap of 14 days. Evaluate at day 7 via `rvr stats --period 7d --detailed --json`; re-check at day 10 and 14 — whichever fires first wins.

CLOCK PEG (codified 2026-06-09): the soak clock pegs to the most recent stable release that CHANGED AGENT-FACING BEHAVIOR — not to every tag. Patch/security releases that don't change agent-facing behavior (per project.patchPolicy) do NOT reset it. Worked example: v1.2.0 (2026-06-09) changed agent-facing behavior → clock starts there; the same-day v1.2.1 (security) and v1.2.2 (perf/quality, no feature surface) patches did NOT reset it. So the v1.2.x soak checkpoints from 2026-06-09: day-7 2026-06-16, re-check day-10, hard cap 2026-06-23.

EXIT GATE (single machine, transport-agnostic, ALL five required):
1. >=150 instrumented calls in the 7d window, test traffic discounted (#130-class leaks, e.g. reverie_init floods).
2. Activity on >=5 distinct days of the window — derive from telemetry timestamps: `jq -r '(.ts/1000|strftime("%F"))' ~/.reverie/telemetry.jsonl | sort -u` (UTC days; bursts don't fake sustained usage).
3. >=5 namespaces written across.
4. >=3 distinct projects active.
5. >=7 elapsed days.
SOFT SIGNAL (check, don't gate): both fleet agents (fable + sol) present in stats agentBreakdown — single-agent signal means the theme-pick generalizes less. Post-#138 ambient detection: unconfigured machines report generic harness names (claude-code/codex, agentDetected:true) — read fable≡claude-code and sol≡codex as one harness class when checking this signal.
Session counts are NOT criteria on either surface: MCP lost ambient traffic (shell-less surfaces only), and CLI sessions are per-process phantoms until harness-free session derivation ships (the #119 leftover). MCP coverage is likewise not soak-measured — it's a deliberate pre-release exercise per [[project.surfaceStrategy]] consequence (a).

Gate met → exit early, run theme-pick (v1.14 playbook Phase 2). 14d reached with thin signal → ship the smallest scoped theme + carry candidates forward; do NOT extend — longer soaks overfit whichever signal happened to surface and batch more fixes than one release can digest.

CALIBRATION (N=1, still v1.14-anchored): v1.14 exited day 12; single-host 7d snapshot at exit: 16 MCP sessions, 281 calls, 7 namespaces, 4 projects. The 150-call bar scales the old 10-session criterion through that snapshot (10/16 × 281 ≈ 175, rounded down for leak discounting); the 5-day bar is untested against history. Refine both with the first post-fleet soak. Gate is deliberately single-machine — cross-machine telemetry isn't aggregable from one host today (v1.15+ candidate: stats --import / merge tool).
